leading_positions.synthesis: Both supporters name the same three laureates (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith) and cite the new solution-processed semiconductor class, the rise from a few percent to over 25 percent efficiency, and independent replication. Both also state the same open issues: stability, lead toxicity and the exclusion of Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis. Aqvist ranks B016 only as a second alternative and Brzezinski, Somfai and Aili raise maturity or attribution objections, so this is the only configuration held by more than one member, and still two of eight.

Aili prefers Cullis and Langer for lipid nanoparticle delivery, citing approved products and chemical specificity. Sparr names B045 as her main alternative but with Cullis, Hope and Madden, and rejects the Langer pairing. Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou accept the impact and maturity but question who is decisive and the proximity to the 2023 Medicine prize.

Aqvist prefers Car and Parrinello, with the cleanest two-person attribution on the shortlist. Sparr lists it as an alternative. Aili, Linke and Zou ask what is distinct from the 1998 and 2013 computational prizes and how far Born-Oppenheimer MD has displaced the original scheme.

Somfai prefers Buchwald and Hartwig for C-N coupling, with mature and tidy attribution. Aqvist keeps it as a reserve and Brzezinski shares the concern about overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

Sparr prefers Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen for phase separation as a physical-chemical principle. Linke ranks it as a first alternative, while Linke, Somfai and Zou question the settled status of the in vivo picture and whether it is chemistry or cell biology.

Brzezinski prefers Gray and Winkler for protein electron tunneling. Aqvist and Zou regard it as well attributed and rigorous but potentially a completion of the 1992 Marcus prize, and Brzezinski himself says opening support was limited to his own ranking.

Chabes proposes a two-part prize: sequencing chemistry (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) and base editing (Liu), three laureates in total. Somfai and Aili keep B012 as an alternative, Aqvist ranks B031 fifth, and several members question genomics versus chemistry and the parallel lineages (Mayer, Ju, Rothberg; Nishida, Kondo).

areas_of_agreement: All eight members name exactly one preferred configuration of at most three laureates, and none of the eight proposes a second configuration that exceeds the three-person limit.
Members across fields accept the scientific importance of B016, B045, B029 and B043, and most disagreements are about attribution, maturity and prior prizes rather than validity.
For B016, the two supporters and Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou all use the Miyasaka, Park, Snaith trio when naming laureates, and Brzezinski calls the impact not in doubt.
Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes all recognise that B045 has demonstrated clinical consequence and exceptional maturity.
B043 appears as an alternative in four files (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou), with several members saying clinical proof or credit division is the obstacle.
scientific_disputes: B069: whether the thermodynamic framework of condensates is established enough to be a chemistry principle when the physiological reality of many specific in vivo assemblies is contested (Linke, Somfai, Zou versus Sparr).

B029: whether the Car-Parrinello fictitious-dynamics scheme is still a lasting conceptual advance given the use of Born-Oppenheimer ab initio MD, and whether a third computational prize since 1998 is acceptable (Aqvist, Aili, Linke, Zou).
B016: whether the core discovery is the absorber and its photophysics, as Linke and Zou argue, or whether device engineering makes it physics or materials science, as Linke notes and Somfai says.
B062 and B052: whether each is a distinct achievement or a sequel to the 1992 Marcus electron-transfer prize and the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
B012 and B031: whether sequencing-by-synthesis and base editing count as chemistry rather than genomics or genome engineering, and whether Medicine would claim them.
attribution_disputes: B016: Miyasaka, Park and Snaith are the common trio, but Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are acknowledged by Linke, Zou, Aqvist and Somfai as having credible claims, and Gratzel's dye-cell lineage blurs priority.

B045: Aili proposes Cullis and Langer, Sparr proposes Cullis, Hope and Madden, and the files disagree on whether the lipidoid and combinatorial strand (Anderson, Langer) or the ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing strand is decisive.
B012: Chabes names Balasubramanian and Klenerman (dropping Mayer); Somfai, Aili and Aqvist point to Mayer, Ju and Rothberg as parallel routes.
B031: Chabes names Liu alone and excludes trainees; Aqvist notes that Nishida and Kondo's cytidine-deaminase fusion is an independent precedent.
B069: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen leave out Pappu and Mittag, whom Sparr, Zou and Linke identify as supplying sequence-level physical chemistry.
B043: the PROTAC line (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and the cereblon glue line (Handa, Ito) have different protagonists, and Somfai, Brzezinski and Zou say a three-person cut cannot cover both.
maturity_disputes: B016: Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes treat the lack of proven stability, lead handling and commercial modules as an early-recognition problem; Linke and Zou argue the prize concerns the discovery and a decade of replication, not product deployment.
B043: Aqvist, Aili, Brzezinski, Chabes and Somfai say clinical proof is still pending, and Chabes says he moved it up to his first alternative.
B031: Chabes concedes base editing is about a decade old and safety is unknown, and Aqvist would hold it until the clinical record is longer.
B069: the field is young and the in vivo interpretation is unsettled; Sparr treats this as normal for a young field and Linke and Zou do not.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Aqvist: biomolecular simulation, QM/MM and EVB work close to B029 field; no tie to Car or Parrinello; declared as field overlap, not a recusal ground.

Brzezinski: own field of electron and proton transfer in respiratory enzymes is close to B062; also a Stockholm University colleague of Zou (relevant to B001, no longer Zou's preferred choice); no recusal sought.
Chabes: own research relies on sequencing and nucleotide pool measurements, which could bias him toward B012; no tie to credited persons.
Sparr: research on lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly is close to B069 and B045; field bias toward soft matter declared; no recusal sought.
Aili: sympathetic to delivery technologies through translational and biomaterials interests (B045); no tie to the Vancouver, MIT or Alnylam groups.
Linke (chair): physics bias toward device and limit-based arguments; adjacent to semiconductor photophysics but no tie to perovskite groups; no recusal sought.
Zou: knows the porous-materials community behind B001 professionally; no stated collaboration with any credited person.
Somfai: no conflict for B052; shares Lund with Linke and Sparr, which no member treats as a recusal issue for these candidates.
questions_for_round2: B016: is the Miyasaka, Park, Snaith trio acceptable, or must Gratzel, Seok or Kanatzidis displace one of them? Is stability and lead toxicity a reason to wait in 2026, or is the discovery of the absorber and its photophysics sufficient (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai versus Linke, Zou)?

B045: who holds the decisive step, ionizable lipids with rapid-mixing formulation (Cullis, Hope, Madden) or the broader delivery and lipidoid concept (Langer, Anderson)? Is Aili's pair or Sparr's trio the right cut, and how should the 2023 Medicine prize be handled in the citation?

B029: which specific results depend on the fictitious-dynamics formulation as opposed to Born-Oppenheimer MD, and does that separate the discovery from the 1998 and 2013 computational prizes (question to Aqvist)?

B043: can the credit be limited to three names without excluding a decisive contributor, and is the clinical record yet sufficient? Should Handa or Ciulli complete a trio if the committee prefers this topic (question to Chabes, Aqvist, Somfai, Zou)?
B069: does Sparr's citation wording stay in physical chemistry, and is omitting Pappu and Mittag defensible?
B062 and B052: what would each citation say that the 1992 Marcus prize and the 2010 cross-coupling prize do not already say (questions to Brzezinski and Somfai)?
B012 and B031: which two names are non-negotiable for sequencing, and would the committee accept a two-part prize pairing it with Liu, or prefer B012 alone, as Chabes suggests?
Does any single configuration have a realistic path to five of eight votes, or should round 2 test combinations of two parts (for example B016 with B045 or B043)?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows eight preferred configurations among seven distinct positions; the only overlap is B016, explicitly preferred by two members (Linke, Zou). No configuration is yet close to the five-vote majority. Disagreement concentrates on attribution (B016, B045, B012, B043) and maturity (B016, B043, B031), with prior-prize overlap (B029, B052, B062) as a recurring third theme. I am one of the two B016 supporters and have tried to describe the other positions on their own terms.
